summary: A short report with a graph of how busy the BBN and USC-ISI TENEX computers were during the working week in July 1973, shown as average load by hour of the day. The author notes that reading such data is tricky and offers a few observations for the network community.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC graphs weekday load averages for BBN and ISI TENEX systems during July 1973. The author notes patterns in the graph but cautions that interpreting the data is difficult.

questions: how busy were arpanet hosts in 1973
how does computer load vary during the day
subtitle: Weekday hourly load averages for two TENEX systems in July 1973.

tldr.problem: The RFC presents utilization data for BBN and ISI TENEX systems that may interest the network community.
tldr.mechanism: A graph plots weekday hourly load averages for July 1973 against time of day in Eastern Daylight Time.
tldr.outcome: The author offers cautious observations, noting that load data alone cannot distinguish more users from more demanding users.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 546's status as Unknown. The RFC presents a dated utilization graph and the author's observations.

sections.title: What Load Average Measures
sections.content:
The RFC presents weekday hourly load averages for the BBN-TENEX and USC-ISI hosts in July 1973. It defines TENEX load average as an average of the number of runnable processes over a period of time, which measures CPU demand.

Time of day in the graph is Eastern Daylight Time.
sections.plainLanguage: Load average measures the average number of processes ready to run. The graph shows this measure by hour for two TENEX systems.

sections.title: Patterns Across the Day
sections.content:
The author says the BBN and ISI curves have approximately the same shape without a time skew. He observes increases as users begin work, a dip around a coffee break, an afternoon peak, and changes around dinner and evening activity.

The RFC presents these as interpretations of the plotted data and says interpretation is tricky.
sections.plainLanguage: The curves rise and fall at times the author associates with users' daily schedules. He presents these as observations, not a definitive explanation.

sections.title: Comparing BBN and ISI
sections.content:
The RFC says the ISI curve is smoother than BBN's and suggests West Coast users may contribute to that pattern. It also says BBN was more heavily loaded during July.

Because the data did not include the number of active jobs, the author says it cannot show whether BBN had more users or more demanding users.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN's system was more heavily loaded in the reported data. The RFC cannot tell whether that was due to more users or heavier jobs.
